subject: Color by X Axis Absolute Value (geom_density)

messages.author: 2a4b5dfb55017d91
messages.subject: Color by X Axis Absolute Value (geom_density)
parts:
I apologize if this question has been answered previously but I was unable to find anything.  

I am plotting a density of the percent of bias of estimates from a simulation.  Something like...

Difference <- ((Estimate - Truth)/Truth)*100

ggplot(RTable2, aes(x = Difference)) 
+ geom_density(aes(kernel = "gaussian"))

What I've been trying to achieve is a color gradient that goes by the absolute value of the X-Axis.  So, basically I will want any part of the line that is near 0 to be green (for example) and then have points become more red (for example) as they get further from zero in absolute value.

Any help or general direction would be very much appreciated!

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Color by X Axis Absolute Value (geom_density)
parts:
Hi:

You can't use geom_density() to do this because it uses geom_ribbon()
and the latter does not allow gradient fill. One alternative is to use
geom_segment() on very small intervals of x and fill the segments
individually. Here is an example from a thread started by Leo Lahti in
this group on Oct. 18:

DF <- rnorm(1000)
library(ggplot2)

# Save the geom_density plot as an object
p <- ggplot(DF, aes(x = x)) + geom_density()

# Extract the data part from the constructed graph
dfp <- ggplot_build(p)$data[[1]]

# Define the x-width of each interval
delta <- diff(dfp$x)[1]

# Replot using geom_segment() instead
ggplot(dfp) +
geom_segment(aes(x = x - delta/2, xend = x + delta/2,
y = ymin, yend = ymax, color = x)) +
scale_color_gradient2()

You'll undoubtedly need to make a few adjustments for your particular
case re the choice of gradient scale function and/or the argument
values to pass, but this is the general idea. See
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/ to find help + examples re the scale
functions.

Dennis
